about.title: Personal Injury Help in Laguna Hills, California
about.longDescription: Laguna Hills sees its share of everyday traffic risk, like most Orange County communities built around busy commuter corridors. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 140 injury collisions, resulting in 208 people injured and 2 traffic deaths. Much of that traffic funnels through I-5 (San Diego Freeway), Alicia Parkway, Paseo De Valencia, and Moulton Parkway — corridors that carry heavy volume throughout the week, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, or in any other kind of accident around town, we can help. We handle personal injury claims and can review what happened. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You focus on healing; let us sort through the claim details. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't commit you to anything.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That means your claim isn't automatically capped just because your injuries are hard to put a price on.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we recover money on your behalf. That structure lets you get legal help without paying anything out of pocket first.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Laguna Hills?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like a city or county vehicle, was involved, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. It's worth getting your situation reviewed sooner rather than later so you don't miss a filing window.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Laguna Hills?
items.answer: Based on public crash records, higher volumes of reported collisions occur along I-5 (San Diego Freeway), Alicia Parkway, Paseo De Valencia, and Moulton Parkway. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Wednesdays between roughly 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the crash. Your total recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't barred outright. We can help sort out how fault might be allocated in your specific case.

items.question: Do you charge anything to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review, and there's no obligation. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover money for you.

items.question: Will I owe money if my case doesn't result in a settlement?
items.answer: We work on contingency, which means we only get paid if we recover money for you. If there's no settlement or award, you typically don't owe attorney fees for the work done on your claim.
